title: rescue-unterminated-json-with-flushable-checkpoints-and-sentinel-debounce
author: Jonas Meyer
description:
Problem:
Clients observed occasionally truncated/unterminated JSON blobs when SSE events were split across network frames and the reassembly heuristics emitted duplicate delimiters or dropped the trailing token. This caused structured output parsing (tool/function call handoff) to fail intermittently in high-latency paths and during churned streaming (keep-alive heartbeats interleaving).

Root causes identified:
- The streamer emitted event delimiters aggressively which could produce duplicate trailing delimiters when a fragment replay occurred; duplicate delimiters confuse downstream JSON assemblers and some OpenAI-compat clients.
- Reassembly preferred the first-arrived fragment instead of a later, more-complete fragment when seq windowing jitter occurred. That led to truncated JSON being forwarded instead of waiting a short, configurable grace window.
- There was no lightweight in-stream marker that operators or the client SDK could use to checkpoint a safely-closed JSON scope when the model emits structured output (objects/arrays) across frames.

What this PR does (high level):
1) Introduces a flushable-checkpoint marker emitted by the producer when it detects a closed JSON value boundary (internal heuristic documented in code). This marker is an opaque SSE event ("x-rw-checkpoint") that does not change user-facing payloads but allows reassembly to commit a fragment as "complete" before advertising to higher layers.
2) Adds sentinel debouncing: the SSE emitter now suppresses emitting duplicate trailing newline/delimiter events for the same logical token when a replay or retransmit is detected within a small time window. The debounce is conservative and configurable via STREAM_SSE_DEBOUNCE_MS.
3) Updates the reassembly logic to prefer a later fragment if a seq-id mismatch occurs within a small lookahead window (150ms by default). This reduces stale-first selection in jittery networks. There is also an explicit max-hold budget so we never stall beyond the configured latency SLO.
4) Adds integration tests that simulate interleaved heartbeats, delayed fragments, and replayed frames from a TCP simulator to ensure structured output (tool calls) are always either delivered complete or clearly marked as incomplete to the consumer.
5) Adds an adapter fallback in openai_compat that recognizes the new checkpoint event and uses it to validate structured outputs before invoking toolcall logic. If a checkpoint is missing but the fragment is older than max-hold, the adapter will perform a conservative retry path rather than invoking incomplete tool calls.

Files changed (summary):
- sse/emitter.py: add checkpoint emission and debounce timer, config knobs for debounce/ms.
- sse/reassembler.rs: rework seq-window selection, add max_hold budget, expose checkpoint recognition.
- openai_compat/adapter.go: understand x-rw-checkpoint and conservative fallback.
- integration_tests/sse_fragmenting_test.py: new deterministic test harness for replay/heartbeat scenarios.
- docs/sse-checkpoints.md: design note and opt-in configuration.
- api/compat/CHANGELOG.md: entry.
- pkg/metrics/streaming_metrics.go: add checkpoint and debounce counters for observability.

Why this is safe:
- The checkpoint event is an internal marker and is ignored by existing clients (SSE consumers that only parse data events). It is not surfaced as part of the generated model text.
- Debounce defaults are conservative (30ms) and guarded by feature-flagging; behavior can be toggled via env vars for canary rollout.
- Reassembly changes fall back to previous behavior if the lookahead window is zero; the max-hold budget prevents pathological head-of-line blocking.

Testing performed:
- Unit tests for emitter debounce logic and checkpoint insertion heuristics.
- Rust-level unit tests for reassembler selection with simulated seq jitter and partial frames.
- End-to-end integration test using the fragmenting_test harness that reproduces the customer-reported failure mode; validated both with and without the openai_compat adapter.
- Benchmark smoke to ensure no measurable increase in median latency (95th percentile unchanged within noise).

Release notes: "Fix intermittent malformed/partial JSON emission in SSE streams by introducing flushable checkpoints, sentinel debounce, and jitter-aware reassembly. Improves stability of structured output and tool/function calling under network jitter."

Risks and followups:
- Some third-party clients that introspect SSE event names might observe the new x-rw-checkpoint event; we documented it as internal and will monitor telemetry for adoption or unexpected behavior.
- Follow-up work: expose a per-route opt-out for checkpoints for extreme ultra-low-latency customers and add an observability dashboard for checkpoint hit/miss rates (ENG-1473).

- [x] Feature-flag + env config for rollout

review_comments: Asha Patel (reviewer): Can you explain how the checkpoint heuristic decides a JSON value is closed? We should avoid false positives with multi-step toolcall payloads.

Jonas Meyer (author): The heuristic looks for balancing of object/array braces at the event boundary and a short lookahead to ensure no immediate continuation token follows. It's conservative and only emits a checkpoint when braces balance and the next token is not a continuation indicator. I'll add comments and a unit test to show behavior on nested structured outputs.

Marcelo Ruiz (reviewer): The new lookahead preference is reasonable but we need an integration test that simulates the exact jitter pattern reported by SRE (retransmit on second fragment). Please add test and telemetry counters.

Jonas Meyer (author): Added deterministic jitter scenario in integration_tests and exported debounce/checkpoint counters to streaming_metrics. Also added a feature-flag env var STREAM_SSE_CHECKPOINT_ENABLED.
Evelyn Cho (reviewer): Small nit: expose the debounce ms via config rather than hard-coding. Also please add a changelog entry and short docs for operators.
Jonas Meyer (author): Switched to env config STREAM_SSE_DEBOUNCE_MS and added docs/changelog per request.
Asha Patel (approver): Verified integration test reproduces the failure pre-change and is fixed post-change. Approving for squash-merge.
Marcelo Ruiz (approver): Ran canary in staging with feature-flag and saw checkpoint hit-rate ~98% for the reproducer without latency regression. Approving.
Merge bot: CI passed on re-run and changelog entry lint OK. Merging via squash.
